Anya (support): Heads-up — customer reported SSE stream that stalls ~30s after auth token refresh. They see a partial last chunk, then connection stays open but no more events. Repro steps attached below.

Liam (eng-runtime): Can you paste the client repro and server logs?

Anya (support): Repro from customer (very small):
```bash
# open SSE with short token TTL ~60s
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer <short-ttl-token>\" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?session=abc\"
```
They say: after ~55–65s the client gets a partial event (truncated JSON) then silence. If client reconnects with Last-Event-ID they sometimes get the rest, sometimes get duplicates.

Anya (support): Server side log snippet (redacted):
```
[2026-03-15T10:12:20Z] conn=789 connected session=abc token_expiry=2026-03-15T10:13:20Z
[2026-03-15T10:13:21Z] auth=refresh session=abc token_ok new_token=tok_renewed
[2026-03-15T10:13:21Z] stream=write conn=789 bytes=742 partial_frame=true
[2026-03-15T10:13:21Z] kvcache=evict session=abc reason=token_rotate
[2026-03-15T10:13:52Z] conn=789 silent-interval=31s last_write=2026-03-15T10:13:21Z
[2026-03-15T10:13:52Z] conn=789 keepalive-ping-sent
```
Anya (support): Customer also saw auth refresh events in audit logs coinciding with the partial writes.

Liam (eng-runtime): Interesting — \"partial_frame=true\" + kvcache eviction on token rotate is suspicious. Could be we flush the KV cache during auth refresh which invalidates prefix state and leaves the connection with an incomplete in-flight chunk. Does the runtime abort streaming write or keep the socket open?

Diego (eng-sre): I can confirm runtime code path: on token rotate we trigger a session refresh hook that may call eviction sync. There was a bug where we call write with non-atomic buffer and don't finalize the SSE chunk on eviction. Need to reproduce locally with short TTL.

Nina (support): Workaround for customers: increase token TTL OR ensure client reconnects on partial frames by treating chunked JSON as incomplete and retry. Also we can suggest set header `X-Stream-Mode: preserve` to use the older stable path while we patch.

Liam (eng-runtime): For repro I ran:
```js
// node repro
const es = require('eventsource');
const s = new es('https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?session=abc', { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer short' } });
s.onmessage = e => console.log('MSG', e.data);
s.onerror = e => console.error('ERR', e);
```
With TTL=60s I saw same behavior: final message logged as `{\"text\": \"incomplete...` then nothing. If I manually reconnect with Last-Event-ID sometimes backend replays partial event fragments.

Liam (eng-runtime): Minimal fix candidate: ensure runtime always emits a terminal newline and `\n\n` after any chunk before eviction path, or move token refresh off the hot path (async rotate) so we don't evict while write is in progress.

Diego (eng-sre): Ops note: rolling deploy of runtime v5.14 happened earlier today; deploy-bot shows canary started at 2026-03-15T09:55:00Z and finished 10:05:00Z. Could be a regression.

deploy-bot: canary deploy v5.14 -> completed (canary 3/3), rollout started.

Anya (support): Customer asked if this could cause billing anomalies (partial responses billed). They see charged tokens for the truncated payload and sometimes duplicates after reconnect.

Diego (eng-sre): Short-term billing mitigation: tag events originating from pre-fix runtime and run a dedupe for reconnect replay windows for affected accounts. I'll open a billing ticket.

Liam (eng-runtime): I'll put up a tiny hotfix: ensure write path calls `flushChunk()` with atomic completion before any eviction/rotate hook. Will run a canary flag gated behind `X-Stream-Mode: preserve=false` for testing.

Anya (support): ETA on canary? Customer is asking for ETA or workaround.

Liam (eng-runtime): Can try to build + canary today; if tests pass we can push safe rollback. ETA ~6 hours.

Nina (support): I'll offer customer TTL increase and client-side Last-Event-ID robust handling as interim. Also asked them for connection traces and `tcpdump` / browser console logs.

Anya (support): Adding repro artifacts to the ticket: network pcap + server logs.

Diego (eng-sre): Follow-up actions: 1) Liam to push hotfix canary. 2) I will create billing-adjust ticket and flag affected accounts. 3) Support to notify customer with interim mitigations. 4) Postmortem if rollout caused regression.

Liam (eng-runtime): Filed PR #4321 with `flushChunk()` fix. Triggering canary deploy now.

Anya (support): Thanks — I'll update the customer and escalate if they want a temporary credits/billing adjustment. :thumbsup:

Diego (eng-sre): If anyone needs to reproduce locally, use header `X-Debug-SSE: trace` to enable verbose runtime tracing in logs.

Nina (support): Marking thread P1 since customer has production impact.

Anya (support): Closing loop here once canary is green or billing ticket created.
